item-125.rationale: Capacity halved 10->5 at t=500 vs path always at 5 (5 seeds, settled window t>=1000): throughput ratio ~1.0, queue ratio 0.97-1.04, loss difference ~0pp. All within the 80% / 1.25x / 2pp thresholds.

item-178.rationale: The trend term 0.08*(e - prev_e) shifts both responses, so the ratio falls below 2 whenever the previous error was latency above setpoint, e.g. down 0.08 vs up 0.14. 65/680 plant-reached and 21/112 synthetic cases fail.

item-191.rationale: On a setpoint change the observation state resets, but the volatility reserve from pre-change variance is released into the output limit. The first post-change correction therefore differs with pre-change history (-4.26 / -4.17 / -4.02 for history sd 0/3/8). Later corrections match.

item-192.rationale: In 6 of 10 seeds, after the capacity halves the controller reads the rise in RTT as a change in path delay ('path-delay-change' rebase of base_rtt). It then settles at about 4.3x the queueing of a path that always had the lower capacity, even over t=1500-2900. This breaks the 1.25x queueing bound.

item-219.rationale: A standard flow sharing with this controller gets only 0.54-0.65 of the throughput it gets beside another standard flow (5 seeds, both start orders). That is well below the 80% threshold.

item-244.rationale: The signal is an EWMA of past errors, not the current deviation. In plant-reached and synthetic states, a +d latency deviation can even raise the limit while -d raises it more, so down > 2*up fails in many states (43/112 synthetic cases).

item-357.rationale: Crossing-setpoint ramps pass, but 36 of 288 random latency multisets give improving order a limit <= worsening order (sorted descending vs ascending, with setpoint-level pre-history). An example is latencies above setpoint after 30 ticks at setpoint. The filtered-error and volatility terms put more weight on older samples.

item-394.rationale: The response is multiplicative with down/up weight DOWN_RATIO/(1+TREND_GAIN) >= 2.67, and vf and af only widen it. The MIN_FACTOR clamp never binds below 2x the up cap. 0 failures across plant-reached, synthetic and ramp states for d in 1-60%.

item-399.rationale: After reaching max_limit and staying there 1, 10, 50 or 300 more ticks, the first response to excursions of 105-250 ms is identical across durations. It scales with the error and is capped by SIGNAL_CAP. There is no saturation-dependent accumulator (the limit is the only integrated quantity).

item-416.rationale: After capacity halving vs always-low capacity (5 seeds): throughput ratio ~1.0, queue ratio 0.48-1.09, loss difference within +/-0.15pp.

item-448.rationale: The limit itself is the clamped integrator, with no windup state. The first response to an excursion after 1, 10, 50 or 300 ticks at max_limit is identical across durations and grows with the error, clipped at ERR_CLIP.

item-456.rationale: The limit uses only the instantaneous error (weighted_error is computed but unused). Improving-order sequences end lower than worsening order in most tests, e.g. 1.2 vs 91 for a 140->60 vs 60->140 ramp.

item-465.rationale: Fails for 78/300 random latency multisets and for one-sided ramps after setpoint pre-history: improving order ends lower than worsening order, e.g. 7.2 vs 9.3. The multiplicative integral with a volatility risk term weights early samples heavily.

item-472.rationale: Mean completion-time ratio over many start phases is <=1.16 for sizes 50-500 and on 10/40-packet buffers. For 20-packet flows on the default path the 10-seed average is about 1.26, right at the 1.25 threshold, and single start phases vary widely. The verdict depends on the exact short-flow scenario.

item-477.rationale: Over t>=1500 (10 seeds) throughput ratio ~1.0, queue ratio <=1.16, loss difference ~0. One seed showed 1.85x queueing in t=1000-2000, but that was a slow transient that settles.

item-485.rationale: Improving order ends higher than worsening order for all crossing ramps, one-sided ramps (with and without pre-history) and 300 random multisets. Only ties occurred, both pinned at min_limit.

item-508.rationale: The standard flow gets 1.38-1.54x its throughput beside another standard flow (5 seeds, both orders), well above 80%.

item-532.rationale: Base RTT doubling at t=500: throughput after the change is 0.99-0.995 of the unchanged run (5 seeds).

item-535.rationale: The standard flow gets 1.55-1.72x its throughput beside another standard flow, above the 80% threshold.

item-568.rationale: In closed loop (seeds 0-5, var_scale pairs 0.2/1 through 0.5/4), the higher-variance workload always converges to a higher mean limit, by +1 to +3.5. Volatility only shrinks correction size.

item-572.rationale: After capacity halving vs always-low capacity: throughput ~1.0, queue ratio 0.67-1.05, loss difference within +/-0.19pp.

item-610.rationale: After capacity halving vs always-low capacity: throughput 1.0, queue ratio 0.997-1.007, loss difference 0.

item-618.rationale: The standard flow gets 1.50-1.65x its throughput beside another standard flow, above 80%.

item-625.rationale: Closed loop, 6 seeds, 1500-tick tails: the higher-variance workload converges to a higher limit in every seed for var_scale 0 vs 1 (default sd=10), 0.5 vs 1 and 1 vs 1.5. It is lower only at larger variances.

item-650.rationale: From a neutral state the ratio is 4x. But the trend term C*(s_new - s) adds in the same direction for both signs, so after even one tick at 5% above setpoint a +/-1% deviation gives down/up ~1.77 (<2). 11/112 synthetic states fail.

item-667.rationale: Averaged over start phases and seeds, short standard flows finish in 0.48-0.61x the time they take beside a standard flow.

item-670.rationale: Improving order ends strictly higher in all crossing ramps, one-sided ramps and 253 non-degenerate random multisets. The only ties occurred with both runs pinned at min_limit.

item-691.rationale: After base RTT doubles, throughput collapses to about 2.5% of the no-change run (0.25 vs 10 packets/tick).

item-699.rationale: Averaged over start phases, short flow completion-time ratio is 0.58-0.66, well under 1.25.

item-753.rationale: Closed loop, 6 seeds: the higher-variance workload converges to a higher mean limit for every var_scale pair tested (0.2/1, 1/2, 1/3, 0.5/4).

item-760.rationale: Down gain is 3x up gain, and the per-tick caps (0.6 vs 0.15) keep down > 2*up. The trend and std terms shift both responses but did not break the 2x margin. 0 non-clamped failures across plant-reached, synthetic and ramp states.

item-820.rationale: Gain switches on a risk signal that includes the prior filtered error, std and derivative, not the current deviation. After a tick at 5% above setpoint, a -1% deviation raises the limit more than a +1% deviation lowers it. 37/112 synthetic states fail, plus one plant state (setpoint_step t=122).

item-827.rationale: Default path: mean short-flow completion ratio 1.15-1.23, just under the threshold, with individual start phases up to 2x. On a 10-packet buffer (path parameters can change per the task) the ratio is 1.59-1.76, a clear violation.

item-833.rationale: Integrates an EWMA of errors (KD=0), so older observations accumulate more weight. Improving order ends lower than worsening order in most tests, e.g. 31.1 vs 38.1.

item-840.rationale: Corrections use the EMA of past errors and the gain sign follows the EMA, not the current deviation. After a stretch below setpoint, a +d deviation still raises the limit (down negative), so down > 2*up fails.

item-863.rationale: Higher variance gives a lower limit for larger variances. But for var_scale 0 vs 1 and 0.5 vs 1 the higher-variance workload converged to a higher limit in all 6 seeds, so a strictly lower limit does not hold for every pair.

item-868.rationale: The window is latched at >= 0.8 x its historic peak. After the capacity halves it stays above BDP+buffer, giving 5.9-8.3pp more loss than a path that always had the lower capacity (2pp limit).

item-921.rationale: Code is the standard Reno-style AIMD. After capacity halving: throughput ~1.0, queue ratio 0.98-1.0, loss difference ~0.

item-924.rationale: Improving order ends lower than worsening order in 70/72 ramp tests, e.g. 28.2 vs 42.6.

item-968.rationale: Averaged over start phases (3 seeds), short standard flows take 1.20-1.40x as long beside this flow as beside a standard flow. Every size >= 50 is above 1.25.

item-988.rationale: Default path: the standard flow's queueing delay ratio averages 1.22-1.24, with individual seeds up to 1.28. On a 10-packet buffer it is 1.52-1.56. The delay-based flow keeps a standing queue that the Reno flow never sees drained.

item-997.rationale: Shaped error uses DOWN_RATIO=3, and the boost and target margin only push downward. The KP term analysis gives down - 2*up >= 2d > 0 in every state. 0 failures across plant-reached, synthetic and ramp states.
